alerts.title: Possible TDF nephrotoxicity with back pain and proteinuria
alerts.message: Guidelines list TDF adverse effects including lower back pain, change in urine volume, bone aches, muscle cramps or pain, and exhaustion. Patient on TDF for 6 years presents with persistent dull lower back pain and heavy feeling in both thighs worsening over 4 months, plus trace proteinuria and low-normal serum phosphate (0.78 mmol/L). Evidence for drug attribution: TDF can cause proximal tubulopathy (Fanconi syndrome) presenting with bone pain, muscle cramps, and proteinuria; phosphate level is at lower end of normal. Evidence against: creatinine is normal (112 umol/L), back pain has plausible occupational explanation (truck driving), and proteinuria may be secondary to uncontrolled hypertension. TDF-specific monitoring (creatinine and eGFR every 12 months) is due.

evidence.recommended_action: Perform serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring for TDF toxicity. Evaluate proteinuria with urine protein-to-creatinine ratio. Consider TDF-related tubulopathy if symptoms persist despite occupational management.

alerts.title: TDF renal monitoring gap — eGFR not documented
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring for TDF-experienced patients every 12 months. Patient has been on TDF for 6 years; today's creatinine (112 umol/L) was checked but no eGFR was documented. No prior creatinine results are available to assess trends. Trace proteinuria on urinalysis adds concern for renal function. The clinician's plan does not include eGFR assessment or follow-up renal monitoring beyond the 6-month review.

evidence.recommended_action: Calculate eGFR from today's creatinine result. Schedule renal function monitoring (creatinine and eGFR) at appropriate intervals per TDF monitoring guidelines.

alerts.title: EFV neuromuscular symptoms vs occupational back pain
alerts.message: Guidelines describe EFV persistent CNS toxicity including dizziness and muscle symptoms. Patient on EFV for 6 years reports heavy feeling in both thighs and slightly stiff gait, which could represent EFV-related neuromuscular effects. Evidence against drug attribution: symptoms have plausible occupational cause (long hours driving, cargo loading), no dizziness or insomnia reported, and onset is relatively recent (4 months) despite 6 years on therapy. Guidelines state if EFV-related symptoms persist, substitute EFV with DTG.

evidence.recommended_action: Screen for EFV-related CNS symptoms using the screening tool. If neuromuscular symptoms are attributed to EFV after excluding occupational causes, consider substitution to DTG per guidelines.

alerts.title: Ibuprofen plus TDF and proteinuria increases renal risk
alerts.message: Guidelines list renal disease as a TDF contraindication caution. Patient on TDF with trace proteinuria and uncontrolled hypertension is prescribed PRN ibuprofen, an NSAID that can reduce renal perfusion. TDF itself can cause renal tubular injury; concurrent NSAID use compounds nephrotoxic risk. Creatinine is currently normal but no eGFR is documented to confirm safe renal function. The combination of TDF, suboptensive blood pressure, proteinuria, and regular NSAID use creates compounding renal risk.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess renal function (eGFR) before recommending ongoing NSAID use. Consider non-pharmacological back pain strategies or renal-safe alternatives. Monitor renal parameters closely.
